title: Strongly monotone variational inequalities: fresh operator samples and mean-square distance

description_paragraphs: Public inputs include dimension $d$ and $R_0$, $\beta$, $\varepsilon$, $\mu$, and $\sigma$, together with the stated initial points and feasible-set information. Analytic representations of hidden functions, operators, and matrices are not supplied.

Let $\mathcal H_t$ denote the full history before query t. Conditional on $\mathcal H_t,z_t$, the response $G_t\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfies $\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal H_t,z_t]=F(z_t)$ and $\mathbb E[\|G_t-F(z_t)\|_2^2\mid\mathcal H_t,z_t]\le\sigma^2$. Each call uses an independent fresh sample.

No reusable sample identifier or cross-point sample reuse is available. No mean-square smoothness of sample gradients or operators is additionally assumed. Blocks within a full vector may be correlated.
Exact Euclidean projection onto the known set is allowed. Its calls are recorded separately and excluded from the primary query count.

proofs.title: Return the public initial point.
proofs.body: The public initialization promise gives $\|z_0-z^\star\|\le R_0$. When $\varepsilon\ge R_0$, returning $z_0$ without querying satisfies both the distance target and its mean-square version, deterministically. Query costs are nonnegative, so the minimum is exactly zero.
proofs.scope: All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

proofs.title: Gaussian two-point testing
proofs.body: In one dimension use $F_a(z)=\mu(z-a)$, $a\in\{-4\varepsilon,4\varepsilon\}$, and additive $N(0,\sigma^2)$ noise. Subtract the known $\mu z$ to obtain observations with mean $-\mu a$. Mean-square distance $\le\varepsilon^2$ forces sign-testing error $\le1/16$. The per-sample KL divergence $32\mu^2\varepsilon^2/\sigma^2$ then gives the stated two-point lower bound.
